paragraphs: Unless the context suggests otherwise, references to "we," "us," "our" or the "Company" refer to Kite Realty Group Trust and our business and operations conducted through our directly or indirectly owned subsidiaries, including Kite Realty Group, L.P., our operating partnership (the "Operating Partnership").

Kite Realty Group Trust is a publicly held REIT that, through its majority-owned subsidiary, Kite Realty Group, L.P., owns interests in various operating subsidiaries and joint ventures engaged in the ownership, operation, acquisition, development, and redevelopment of high-quality, open-air, grocery-anchored shopping centers and vibrant mixed-use assets that are primarily located in high-growth Sun Belt markets and select strategic gateway markets in the United States. Following our merger with Retail Properties of America, Inc. ("RPAI") in 2021, we became a top-five open-air shopping center REIT based upon market capitalization. We derive our revenue primarily from the collection of contractual rents and reimbursement payments from tenants under existing lease agreements at each of our properties. Therefore, our operating results depend materially on, among other things, the ability of our tenants to make required lease payments, the health and resilience of the U.S. retail sector, particularly in light of increased tariffs in 2025, interest rate volatility, job growth, the real estate market, and overall economic conditions.

As of December 31, 2025, we owned interests in a portfolio of 167 operating retail/mixed-use properties, including 159 wholly owned properties and eight properties owned through four unconsolidated joint ventures, totaling approximately 26.9 million square feet, excluding (i) two operating retail properties classified as held for sale as of December 31, 2025, (ii) Eastgate Crossing, a 152,682 square foot multi-tenant retail property in the Durham-Chapel Hill MSA that was reclassified from our operating portfolio in September 2025 due to significant disruption caused by severe flooding as a result of Tropical Storm Chantal, and (iii) two standalone office properties with 0.4 million square feet. Of the 167 operating retail/mixed-use properties, 10 contain an office component. We also own interests in one development project that is under construction as of December 31, 2025 and an additional two properties with future redevelopment opportunities. Our operating retail portfolio was 95.1% leased to a diversified retail tenant base, with no single retail tenant accounting for more than 2.6% of our total annualized base rent ("ABR"). In the aggregate, our largest 25 tenants accounted for 25.5% of our ABR. See Item 2, "Properties," for a list of our top 25 tenants by ABR.
•The Company realized net income attributable to common shareholders of $298.7 million for the year ended December 31, 2025;
•The Company generated NAREIT Funds From Operations ("FFO") of $468.6 million and Core Funds From Operations ("Core FFO") of $460.4 million;

•Same Property Net Operating Income ("Same Property NOI") grew by 2.9% in 2025 compared to 2024 primarily due to contractual rent growth and higher base rent driven by positive new and renewal leasing spreads, partially offset by higher bad debt expense;

•In 2025, we executed new and renewal leases on 683 individual spaces representing approximately 4.6 million square feet of retail space, achieving a blended cash leasing spread of 13.8% on 501 comparable leases. The blended cash leasing spread for comparable new and non-option renewal leases was 20.3%;
•Our operating retail portfolio was 95.1% leased as of December 31, 2025, with our anchor leased percentage at 96.7% and our small shop leased percentage at 92.3%;
•Our operating retail portfolio ABR per square foot was $22.63 as of December 31, 2025, an increase of $1.48, or 7.0%, from the prior year; and
•As of December 31, 2025, we derived 79% of our operating retail portfolio ABR from properties with a grocery component, which includes shopping centers with a big box wine and spirits store.
•We ended the year with $1.0 billion of borrowing capacity on our $1.1 billion unsecured revolving credit facility (the "Revolving Facility");

•In June 2025, we completed a public offering of $300.0 million in aggregate principal amount of 5.20% senior unsecured notes due 2032 (the "Notes Due 2032"), the proceeds of which were used to repay the $150.0 million unsecured term loan that was scheduled to mature on July 17, 2026, borrowings on the Revolving Facility, and the $80.0 million principal balance of the 4.47% senior unsecured notes that matured on September 10, 2025;

•In July 2025, we amended the credit agreement related to the Revolving Facility and $300.0 million unsecured term loan that matures in July 2029 (the "$300M Term Loan") to eliminate an additional 0.10% Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") spread adjustment applicable to both instruments. In addition, the amendment reduced the ratings-based pricing credit spread on the $300M Term Loan. We also amended the term loan agreement related to the $250.0 million unsecured term loan that matures in October 2027 (the "$250M Term Loan") to eliminate an additional 0.10% SOFR spread adjustment;
•We acquired Village Commons, a grocery-anchored, multi-tenant retail property in the Miami MSA, for a gross purchase price of $68.4 million in January 2025;

headings: Our business, financial condition, performance, and value are subject to risks and conditions associated with real estate assets and the real estate industry.
Ongoing challenges facing our retail tenants, including bankruptcies, financial instability, and consolidations, could have a material adverse effect on our business.
Elevated levels of inflation may adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.

Joint venture investments could be adversely affected by the structure, terms and activities of our joint venture partners.
We face significant competition and risks in pursuing acquisition opportunities.

We could experience a decline in the fair value of our real estate assets and be subject to impairment charges.

paragraphs: The following factors, among others, could cause actual results to differ materially from those contained in forward-looking statements made in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and presented elsewhere by management from time to time. These factors, among others, may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, operating results and cash flows, including our ability to make distributions to our shareholders. It is not possible to predict or identify all such factors, and this list should not be considered a complete statement of all potential risks or uncertainties.

Our primary business is the ownership, operation, acquisition, development, and redevelopment of high-quality, open-air, grocery-anchored shopping centers and vibrant mixed-use and lifestyle assets in the United States. Our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, per share trading price of our common shares, and ability to satisfy our debt service obligations and make distributions to our shareholders are subject to, and could be materially and adversely affected by, risks associated with acquiring, owning, and operating these types of real estate assets. These risks include events and conditions that are beyond our control, such as periods of economic slowdown or recession, federal government shutdowns, disruptions related to tariffs and other trade or sanction issues, declines in the financial condition of our tenants, natural disasters such as fires, earthquakes, or floods, rising interest rates, difficulty in leasing vacant space or renewing existing tenants, a decline in the value of our assets, or the public perception that any of these events may occur. Additionally, certain costs of our business, such as insurance, real estate taxes, utilities, and corporate expenses, are relatively inflexible and generally do not decrease if a property is not fully occupied, rental rates decline, a tenant fails to pay rent, or other circumstances cause our revenues to decrease. If we are unable to lower our operating costs when revenues decline and/or fully recover cost increases from our tenants, our financial condition, operating results, and cash flows could be materially and adversely impacted.

We derive the majority of our revenue from retail tenants who lease space from us at our properties; therefore, our ability to generate cash from operations is dependent upon the ability of our tenants to pay the base rent, expense recoveries, and other charges due under their leases on a timely basis. The success of our tenants in operating their businesses continues to be impacted by many current economic challenges, which impact their cost of doing business, including, but not limited to, inflation, labor shortages, tariff policies, supply chain constraints, retail theft, violent crime, decreasing consumer confidence and discretionary spending, increasing energy prices, and volatile interest rates. Sustained weakness in certain sectors of the U.S. economy could result in the bankruptcy or weakened financial condition of a number of retailers, including some of our tenants, and an increase in store closures. Tenants may also choose to consolidate, downsize, or relocate their operations for various reasons, including mergers or other restructurings. These events, or other similar events, and economic conditions are beyond our control and could affect the overall economy as well as specific properties in our portfolio and our overall cash flow and results of operations, including the following, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business:

•Collections. Tenants may have difficulty paying their rent and other charges due under their lease agreements on a timely basis or request rent deferrals, reductions, or abatements as a result of operating challenges.

•Leasing. Tenants may delay or cancel lease commencements, decline to extend or renew leases upon expiration, reduce the size of their leased space, close certain locations, or declare bankruptcy, which could result in the termination of the tenant's lease and the related loss of rental income. Such terminations or cancellations could result in lease terminations or reductions in rent by certain other tenants in the same shopping center due to contractual co-tenancy termination or rent reduction rights contained in some leases.

•Re-leasing. We may be unable to re-lease vacated space at attractive rents or at all. In some cases, it may take an extended period of time or increased costs for renovations or concessions to re-lease a space, particularly if it involves a significant tenant or a non-owned anchor tenant in multiple locations.

paragraphs: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the accompanying audited consolidated financial statements and related notes thereto and Item 1A, "Risk Factors," appearing elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. In this discussion, unless the context suggests otherwise, the terms "the Company," "we," "us," and "our" refer to Kite Realty Group Trust and its direct and indirect subsidiaries, including Kite Realty Group, L.P.

In the following overview, we discuss, among other things, the status of our business and properties, the effect that current U.S. economic conditions are having on our retail tenants and us, and the current state of the financial markets and how it impacts our financing strategy.

Kite Realty Group Trust is a publicly held REIT that, through its majority-owned subsidiary, Kite Realty Group, L.P., owns interests in various operating subsidiaries and joint ventures engaged in the ownership, operation, acquisition, development, and redevelopment of high-quality, open-air, grocery-anchored shopping centers and vibrant mixed-use assets that are primarily located in high-growth Sun Belt markets and select strategic gateway markets in the United States. Following our merger with RPAI in 2021, we became a top-five open-air shopping center REIT based upon market capitalization. We derive our revenue primarily from the collection of contractual rents and reimbursement payments from tenants under existing lease agreements at each of our properties. Therefore, our operating results depend materially on, among other things, the ability of our tenants to make required lease payments, the health and resilience of the U.S. retail sector, particularly in light of increased tariffs in 2025, interest rate volatility, job growth, the real estate market, and overall economic conditions.

As of December 31, 2025, we own interests in a portfolio of 167 operating retail/mixed-use properties, including 159 wholly owned properties and eight properties owned through four unconsolidated joint ventures, totaling approximately 26.9 million square feet, excluding (i) two operating retail properties classified as held for sale as of December 31, 2025, (ii) Eastgate Crossing, a 152,682 square foot multi-tenant retail property in the Durham-Chapel Hill MSA that was reclassified from our operating portfolio in September 2025 due to significant disruption caused by severe flooding as a result of Tropical Storm Chantal, and (iii) two standalone office properties with 0.4 million square feet. Of the 167 operating retail/mixed-use properties, 10 contain an office component. We also own interests in one development project that is under construction as of December 31, 2025 and an additional two properties with future redevelopment opportunities.

We continue to monitor the impact of inflation and tariffs on our operating and financial performance. Although inflation has moderated significantly from peak levels experienced during 2022, inflation may increase in the future as a result of multiple factors, including the tariffs implemented by the U.S. government in 2025 on imported goods from specific countries. These tariffs may lead to higher prices for many of the products that our tenants sell, potentially reducing consumer demand and spending and negatively impacting our tenants' sales volume and overall health. This, in turn, has and could in the future put downward pricing pressure on rents that we are able to charge to new or renewing tenants, such that rent spreads and, in some cases, our percentage rents could be adversely impacted. Additionally, uncertainty regarding the scope and duration of the current and potential tariffs can lead to significant business uncertainty, affecting our tenants' strategic planning and store expansion plans. Many of our leases contain provisions designed to mitigate the adverse impact of inflation, including stated rent increases and requirements for tenants to pay a share of operating expenses, including common area maintenance, real estate taxes, insurance, or other operating expenses related to the maintenance of our properties, with escalation clauses in most leases. Over the past few years, we have made significant progress in executing leases that include higher fixed-rent increases while also including consumer price index-based, anti-gouging protection for tenants. However, the stated rent increases or limits on such tenant's obligation to pay its share of operating expenses could be lower than the increase in inflation at any given time. Inflation may also increase labor or other general and administrative expenses, which cannot be easily reduced.

Historically, economic indicators such as GDP growth, consumer confidence, and employment have been correlated with demand for certain of our tenants' products and services. An economic recession could, among other impacts, increase the number of our tenants that are unable to meet their lease obligations to us and limit the demand from new tenants for space in our properties.

Over the past two years, demand for open-air retail real estate has been strong due to the limited availability of desirable retail space and limited new construction over the previous 15 years. As a result, in 2024, we experienced our highest annual leasing activity in the Company's history with approximately 5.0 million square feet of leasing volume, and in 2025, we leased approximately 4.6 million square feet at 13.8% comparable blended cash leasing spreads. Open-air centers are thriving for a variety of reasons, including their ability to function as last-mile fulfillment centers and their convenient and affordable nature for retailers and consumers. Their appeal includes conveniently located and easily accessible parking fields, lower operating expenses as compared to other retail formats, and essential anchors that drive daily trips. In addition, the Company's property types are particularly suited for retailers' current and evolving needs, including curbside pick-up and buying online and picking up in store ("BOPIS"), which we believe will benefit from tenant demand for additional space. The strength of the Company's real estate is further evidenced by our continued strong cash leasing spreads and ABR for the retail portfolio of $22.63 per square foot as of December 31, 2025.

In evaluating potential acquisition, development, and redevelopment opportunities, we look for strong sub-markets where average household income, educational attainment, population density, traffic counts, and daytime workforce populations are above the broader market average. We also focus on locations that are benefiting from current population migratory patterns, namely major cities in business-friendly states with no or relatively low income taxes and mild or temperate climates. In our largest submarkets, household incomes are significantly higher and state income taxes are relatively lower than the medians for the broader markets.

In addition to targeting submarkets with strong consumer demographics, we focus on having the most desirable tenant mix at each shopping center. We have aggressively targeted and executed leases with prominent grocers, including Lidl, Aldi, Whole Foods, Trader Joe's, Sprouts Farmers Market, and BJ's Wholesale Club; expanding retailers such as Nordstrom Rack, Homesense, Ross Dress for Less, Burlington, Sierra, J.Crew Factory, and Boot Barn; service and restaurant retailers; and other retailers such as Ulta Beauty, Barnes & Noble, REI, Five Below, L.L.Bean, and Total Wine & More. Additionally, we have identified cost-efficient ways to relocate, re-tenant, and renegotiate leases at several of our properties, which allows us to attract more suitable tenants.

As part of our portfolio management, in 2025, we began disposing of select properties and land parcels that were no longer core components of our growth strategy and sold a total of $621.7 million of larger-format and other non-core assets. These dispositions have reduced our exposure to at-risk tenants and have elevated the overall quality of our portfolio. We are exploring opportunities to improve the portfolio by identifying and executing additional dispositions of non-core and/or larger-format assets in 2026. We expect to use the net proceeds from these dispositions towards a combination of acquisitions completed via 1031 Exchange, debt reduction, share repurchases, and/or special dividends. In order to allow for additional share repurchases, in February 2026, our Board of Trustees authorized a $300.0 million increase to the size of our Share Repurchase Program, authorizing share repurchases up to a maximum of $600.0 million of our common shares.

In 2025, we maintained a conservative balance sheet and ample liquidity to fund future growth. We ended 2025 with approximately $1.0 billion of combined cash and borrowing capacity on the Revolving Facility. In addition, as of December 31, 2025, we had $410.6 million of debt principal scheduled to mature through December 31, 2026, which we expect will be satisfied through a combination of cash flows generated from operations, capital markets transactions, and borrowings on the Revolving Facility.

The three investment-grade credit ratings we maintain provide us with access to the unsecured public bond market, which we may continue to use in the future to finance acquisitions, repay maturing debt, and maintain steady interest rates.

Effective July 4, 2025, certain changes to U.S. tax law were approved that impact us and our shareholders. Among other changes, this legislation (i) permanently extends the 20% deduction for "qualified REIT dividends" for individuals and other non-corporate taxpayers under Section 199A of the Internal Revenue Code (the "Code"), (ii) increases the percentage limit under the REIT asset test applicable to taxable REIT subsidiaries from 20% to 25% for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025, and (iii) increases the base on which the 30% interest deduction limit under Section 163(j) of the Code applies by excluding depreciation, amortization, and depletion from the definition of "adjusted taxable income" (i.e., based on EBITDA rather than EBIT) for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.

As of December 31, 2025, we own interests in a portfolio of 167 operating retail/mixed-use properties, excluding two operating retail properties classified as held for sale as of December 31, 2025 and Eastgate Crossing, which was reclassified from our operating portfolio in September 2025 due to significant disruption caused by severe flooding as a result of Tropical Storm Chantal. We also own interests in two standalone office properties, one development project that is currently under construction, and two additional properties with future redevelopment opportunities. paragraphs: 除非上下文另有說明，否則提及 "we"、"us"、"our" 或 "the Company" 時，均指 Kite Realty Group Trust 以及我們透過直接或間接擁有之子公司所進行之業務與運作，包括 Kite Realty Group, L.P.，我們的運營合夥企業（"運營合夥企業"）。

Kite Realty Group Trust 是一家公開發行的 REIT，透過其控股子公司 Kite Realty Group, L.P.，擁有各項運營子公司及合資企業的權益，這些子公司及合資企業從事高品質、開放式、附設超市的購物中心及活躍的混合用途資產之擁有、運營、購入、開發與重新開發，這些資產主要位於美國高成長的 Sun Belt 市場及部分戰略門戶市場。在 2021 年與 Retail Properties of America, Inc.（"RPAI"）合併後，我們成為根據市場總市值排名前五的開放式購物中心 REIT。我們的收入主要來自於各個物業現有租賃契約下租戶所支付的契約租金及補償金。因此，我們的營運結果在很大程度上取決於租戶能否履行租賃契約的付款義務、美國零售業的健康與韌性，特別是在 2025 年增加關稅、利率波動、就業成長、房地產市場以及總體經濟狀況等因素的影響下。

截至2025年12月31日，本公司持有167處營運中零售/混合用途不動產的權益，包括159處完全擁有不動產及8處透過四個未合併合資企業所擁有不動產，總計約26.9百萬平方英呎，不計(i)兩處營運中零售不動產，於2025年12月31日被歸類為待售，(ii)Eastgate Crossing，為一處位於Durham-Chapel Hill MSA的152,682平方英呎多租戶零售不動產，因熱帶風暴Chantal造成的嚴重水災導致重大幹擾，於2025年9月重新歸類為非營運資產，以及(iii)兩處獨立辦公室不動產，總計0.4百萬平方英呎。在167處營運中零售/混合用途不動產中，有10處包含辦公室零組件。本公司亦持有1處正在興建中的開發項目權益，以及另外2處具未來重新開發潛力的不動產。本公司營運零售資產的租賃率為95.1%，租賃給多元化的零售租戶，無任何單一零售租戶佔總年化基礎租金（"ABR"）超過2.6%。整體而言，本公司前25大租戶佔總ABR的25.5%。詳見第2項"不動產"，以取得按ABR計算的前25大租戶名單。
•本公司於2025年12月31日財務年度實現歸屬於普通股股東的淨收入為298.7百萬美元；
•本公司產生NAREIT資金從業運作（"FFO"）為468.6百萬美元，以及核心資金從業運作（"Core FFO"）為460.4百萬美元；
•2025 年，相同物業淨營運收入（"Same Property NOI"）相比 2024 年成長 2.9%，主要因契約租金成長及因正面的新租約與續約租賃擴張所導致的基礎租金提高，部分抵銷因壞帳費用增加的影響；
•2025年，本公司執行了683處個別空間的租賃契約，總計約4.6百萬平方英呎的零售空間，達成501處可比租賃契約的平均現金租賃差幅為13.8%。可比新租賃及非選擇權續約租賃的平均現金租賃差幅為20.3%；
•截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的運營零售資產出租率為 95.1%，其中主要租戶出租率為 96.7%，小型商店出租率為 92.3%；
•本公司營運零售資產組合每平方英呎的 ABR 為 22.63 美元，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，較前一年增加 1.48 美元，或 7.0%；
•截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司營運零售資產組合 ABR 中有 79% 來自具食品零組件的資產，包含設有大型酒類與酒飲商店的購物中心；
•本公司於本年結束時，於 11 億美元無擔保循環信用貸款融資（"循環貸款"）下擁有 10 億美元的借款能力；
•2025 年 6 月，本公司完成發行總額 3 億美元的 5.20% 無擔保高收益票據（"2032 年到期票據"），所得資金用於償還原定於 2026 年 7 月 17 日到期的 1.5 億美元無擔保定期貸款、循環貸款的借款，以及 2025 年 9 月 10 日到期的 8,000 萬美元本金的 4.47% 無擔保高收益票據；

•2025 年 7 月，本公司修改與循環貸款及 3 億美元無擔保定期貸款（"3 億美元定期貸款"）相關的信用協議，以消除適用於兩項工具的額外 0.10% 保證過夜融資利率（"SOFR"）調整幅度。此外，修改也降低了 3 億美元定期貸款的評級基準利率調整幅度。本公司亦修改與 2.5 億美元無擔保定期貸款（"2.5 億美元定期貸款"）相關的貸款協議，以消除適用於該貸款的額外 0.10% SOFR 調整幅度；

paragraphs: 以下討論應配合附上的審計合併財務報表及其相關附註，以及本年度報告表10-K中第1A項「風險因素」一節內容一併閱讀。在本討論中，除非文意另有顯示，否則「本公司」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們的」均指Kite Realty Group Trust及其直接與間接子公司，包括Kite Realty Group, L.P。
在以下概覽中，我們討論，包括但不限於我們的業務與資產狀況、當前美國經濟條件對我們零售租戶及我們的影響，以及當前財務市場的狀態及其對我們融資策略的影響。

Kite Realty Group Trust為一家公開上市的REIT，透過其控股子公司Kite Realty Group, L.P.，擁有各項營運子公司與合資公司的權益，這些子公司與合資公司從事高品質、開放式、附設超市的購物中心及活躍的混合用途資產的擁有、營運、購入、開發與重建，這些資產主要位於美國高成長的Sun Belt地區與選擇性的戰略門戶市場。在2021年與RPAI合併後，我們成為根據市值排名前五的開放式購物中心REIT。我們的收入主要來自於現有租賃契約下租戶的合約租金與補償付款的收取。因此，我們的營運結果在很大程度上取決於租戶能否履行租賃付款義務、美國零售業的健康與韌性，特別是在2025年增加關稅、利率波動、就業成長、房地產市場與總體經濟條件的情況下。

我們持續監測通貨膨脹與關稅對我們營運與財務表現的影響。雖然通貨膨脹已顯著緩和，從2022年高峯水平下降，但未來可能因多種因素而增加，包括美國政府在2025年對特定國家進口商品所實施的關稅。這些關稅可能導致我們租戶所銷售的許多產品價格上漲，潛在減少消費者需求與支出，並對租戶的銷售量與整體健康狀況造成負面影響。這會導致我們能向新租戶或續約租戶收取的租金出現向下壓力，使得租金差距，甚至在某些情況下，我們的百分比租金可能受到不利影響。此外，關於當前與潛在關稅範圍與持續時間的不確定性，可能導致重大業務不確定性，影響租戶的戰略規劃與店面擴張計畫。我們許多租賃契約包含設計用以緩解通貨膨脹負面影響的條款，包括明確的租金上漲與租戶需支付部分營運費用的規定，包括公共區域維護、房地產稅、保險或其他與我們資產維護相關的營運費用，大多數租賃契約包含上漲條款。在過去幾年，我們在執行包含較高固定租金上漲的租賃契約方面取得了顯著進展，同時也包含消費者物價指數基準的、保護租戶免於價格暴漲的條款。然而，明確的租金上漲或租戶支付營運費用的限制可能低於任何特定時間點的通貨膨脹幅度。通貨膨脹也可能增加勞動或其他一般及行政費用，而這些費用不容易輕易減少。
歷史上，GDP成長、消費者信心與就業率等經濟指標與我們部分租戶的產品與服務需求有相關性。經濟衰退可能對我們的影響包括增加無法履行租賃義務的租戶數量，並限制新租戶對我們資產空間的需求。

在過去兩年，開放式零售不動產的需求強勁，這是因為優質零售空間的供應有限，且過去15年新興建設有限。因此，在2024年，我們經歷了本公司歷史上最高的年度租賃活動，約500萬平方英呎的租賃量，而在2025年，我們租賃了約460萬平方英呎，平均租賃差距為13.8%。開放式購物中心之所以興旺，是因為它們能作為最後一公里配送中心，且對零售商與消費者而言具有便利與經濟的特性。其吸引力包括 conveniently located 且易於接駁的停車場、相比其他零售形式較低的營運費用，以及能驅動日常出行的必要主力店。此外，本公司資產類型特別適合零售商目前與未來的需要，包括車邊取貨與線上購物、店內取貨（"BOPIS"），我們認為這將受益於租戶對更多空間的需求。本公司不動產的強勢進一步體現在我們持續強勁的租賃差距與ABR，截至2025年12月31日，零售資產的ABR為每平方英呎22.63美元。
在評估潛在的收購、開發與重開發機會時，我們尋找平均家庭收入、教育程度、人口密度、交通流量與日間工作人口均高於廣泛市場平均的強勢次市場。我們也關注受益於當前人口遷移趨勢的地區，即商業友好的州份的大型城市，這些州份無或相對低的所得稅，以及溫和或溫帶氣候。在我們最大的次市場中，家庭收入顯著高於廣泛市場的中位數，而州所得稅相對較低。

除針對具備強大消費族羣的次市場進行目標外，我們亦著重於每個購物中心擁有最理想的租戶組合。我們積極針對並執行與知名蔬果零售商的租賃，包括 Lidl、Aldi、Whole Foods、Trader Joe's、Sprouts Farmers Market 與 BJ's Wholesale Club；擴張型零售商如 Nordstrom Rack、Homesense、Ross Dress for Less、Burlington、Sierra、J.Crew Factory 與 Boot Barn；服務與餐飲零售商；以及其他零售商如 Ulta Beauty、Barnes & Noble、REI、Five Below、L.L.Bean 與 Total Wine & More。此外，我們已識別出成本效益高的方式，於數個物業進行遷移、重新出租與重新談判租約，這使我們能吸引更適合的租戶。

根據我們的資產管理策略，於 2025 年，我們開始處分不再屬於我們成長策略核心組成部分的特定物業與土地，並出售總計 6.217 億美元的較大規模與其他非核心資產。這些處分已降低我們對高風險租戶的敞口，並提升我們資產組合整體品質。我們正在探討於 2026 年進一步識別與執行非核心與/或較大規模資產處分的機會，以改善資產組合。我們預期將使用這些處分所得的淨現金，用於完成 1031 交換的收購、減債、股票回購與/或特別股息。為允許進行更多股票回購，於 2026 年 2 月，我們的董事會授權將股票回購計畫規模增加 3 億美元，授權股票回購上限為 6 億美元的普通股。
於 2025 年，我們維持保守的資產負債表與充足的流動性以支持未來成長。我們於 2025 年底擁有約 10 億美元的現金與信貸融資能力。此外，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們有 4.106 億美元的債務本金預計於 2026 年 12 月 31 日前到期，我們預期將透過營運產生的現金流、資本市場交易與信貸融資來償還。
我們維持的三項投資等級信用評級，使我們能取得無擔保公眾債券市場的融資管道，我們可能在未來繼續使用此管道來資助收購、償還到期債務與維持穩定的利率。

自 2025 年 7 月 4 日起，美國稅法進行了一些變更，影響我們與股東。其中變更包括：(i) 永久延長「合格 REIT 股息」的 20% 折扣，適用於個人及其他非公司納稅人，根據內政部稅收法第 199A 條款；(ii) 將適用於課稅 REIT 子公司的 REIT 資產測試的百分比限制，從 20% 提高至 25%，適用於 2025 年 12 月 31 日後開始的課稅年度；(iii) 將第 163(j) 條款下 30% 利息扣除限制的計算基礎提高，透過排除折舊、攤銷與減損，從「調整後課稅所得」（即基於 EBITDA 而非 EBIT）的定義中排除，適用於 2024 年 12 月 31 日後開始的課稅年度。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們擁有 167 間營運中的零售/混合用途物業的權益，不包括兩間被歸類為待售的營運零售物業，以及 2025 年 9 月因熱帶風暴 Chantal 引起的嚴重水災造成重大幹擾而重新歸類為非營運資產的 Eastgate Crossing。我們也擁有兩間獨立辦公室物業的權益、一間目前正在興建的開發項目，以及兩間未來有重開發潛力的物業。下表顯示截至 2025 年、2024 年與 2023 年 12 月 31 日，我們所擁有的營運物業與開發項目總數：

paragraphs: 下列因素，包括但不限於，可能會導致實際結果與本年度報告表10-K中所作之預測性陳述，以及管理階層不時於其他地方所作之預測性陳述有重大差異。這些因素，包括但不限於，可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果及現金流造成重大不利影響，包括本公司對股東發放紅利的能力。無法預測或識別所有這些因素，此清單不應視為所有潛在風險或不確定性的完整陳述。

本公司主要業務為擁有、營運、取得、開發及重新開發美國境內高品質、開放式、以超市為核心的購物中心及活躍的混合用途與生活方式資產。本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流、普通股每股交易價格，以及履行債務償還義務及對股東發放紅利的能力，皆受取得、擁有及營運這些類型不動產資產相關風險影響，並可能受到重大且不利的影響。這些風險包括我們無法控制的事件與情況，例如經濟減速或衰退期、聯邦政府停擺、與關稅及其他貿易或制裁問題相關的中斷、租戶財務狀況下降、自然災害如火災、地震或洪水、利率上升、難以出租空置空間或續約現有租戶、資產價值下降，或公眾認為這些事件可能發生的觀感。此外，本公司某些營運成本，如保險、不動產稅、公用事業及公司費用，相對缺乏彈性，通常在一個物業未完全出租、租金下降、租戶未支付租金，或其他情況導致收入下降時，這些成本不會減少。若我們無法在收入下降時降低營運成本，或無法完全從租戶處收回成本增加，則本公司財務狀況、營運結果及現金流可能受到重大且不利的影響。

我們的收入主要來自於零售租戶，他們租用我們的物業空間；因此，我們透過營運產生現金的能力，取決於租戶能否按時支付其租約下的基本租金、費用回收及其他應付款項。租戶在經營其業務時，持續受到許多當前經濟挑戰的影響，這些挑戰影響其營運成本，包括但不限於通貨膨脹、人力短缺、關稅政策、供應鏈限制、零售竊盜、暴力犯罪、消費者信心與可支配開支下降、能源價格上升以及利率波動。美國經濟某些領域持續疲軟，可能會導致許多零售商，包括一些租戶，出現破產或財務狀況惡化，並增加商店關閉的情況。租戶也可能因各種原因選擇合併、縮編或遷移其營運，包括合併或其他重組。這些事件，或其他類似事件，以及經濟情況皆超出我們的控制範圍，可能影響整體經濟以及我們資產組閤中的特定物業，以及我們整體現金流與營運結果，包括以下任何一種情況，都可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響：
•收款。租戶可能因營運困難而難以按時支付其租賃契約下的租金及其他應付款項，或請求租金延後、減少或減免。
•租賃。租戶可能延後或取消租賃起始，拒絕在租約到期時續約或延長租約，減少租賃空間規模，關閉某些據點，或聲請破產，這可能會導致租戶租賃契約終止，並導致相關租金收入損失。這些終止或取消，可能會導致同一購物中心內其他租戶終止租賃或減少租金，這是因為某些租賃契約中包含合約共租戶終止或租金減少權條款。
•重新租賃。我們可能無法以具吸引力的租金或任何租金重新租賃空置空間。在某些情況下，重新租賃空間可能需要較長時間或增加裝修或讓利成本，特別是在涉及重要租戶或非自有核心租戶於多個據點的情況下。
